run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T07:32:40Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by HTTP 504 'response_timeout' responses the proxy returned after ~15 s to upstream frontend: over the hour ending 07:47:54Z frontend-proxy ingress spans carried 1349.8 ERROR spans (HTTP 504) versus 17730 UNSET, and the 5-minute error rate jumped from 0 to ~1.9-2.0 errors/s from 07:32:54Z, matching the alert start 07:32:40Z. The slow dependency is product-catalog: checkout's client spans for oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct hit a 15000 ms p95 from 07:33:54Z while product-catalog's own server spans for the same operation stayed at ~1.9-2.0 ms, and frontend's product-catalog client calls collapsed to zero while the product-catalog pod kept serving other callers and logging normally. Chaos-mesh events name the mechanism: Schedule otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay (namespace chaos-mesh) spawned NetworkChaos experiments every minute from 07:30:39Z to 07:38:39Z that were 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9' and recovered ~55 s later. Pods and deployments (frontend-proxy, frontend, checkout, product-catalog) are Ready with 0 restarts, so the failure is a network-path fault around the product-catalog pod, not a crashed or unhealthy workload; the exact delay/peer configuration of the NetworkChaos cannot be read here and the continuation of the injected fault after the last visible event (07:38:39Z) is unverified.

claims.text: frontend-proxy emitted error spans on its ingress operation: over the hour ending 07:47:54Z there were 1349.77 increment of traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",span_name="ingress",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} versus 17729.97 with STATUS_CODE_UNSET, plus 21.34 errors on span 'router frontend egress'.

The frontend-proxy ingress error rate (5m rate of STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans) was 0 up to 07:31:54Z and then rose: 0.50/s at 07:32:54Z, 0.96/s at 07:33:54Z, 1.47/s at 07:34:54Z, ~1.92-2.03/s from 07:35:54Z to 07:41:54Z, then 1.54/s, 1.13/s and 0.63/s at 07:42:54-07:44:54Z; this deviation starts at the alert's 07:32:40Z start.

frontend-proxy logs record the failing requests as '504 UT response_timeout' with upstream 'frontend' and durations of 14999-15000 ms, for example 'GET /api/products/6E92ZMYYFZ HTTP/1.1" 504 UT response_timeout' and 'GET /api/recommendations?productIds=OLJCESPC7Z HTTP/1.1" 504 UT response_timeout'.

The error spans are frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans with status_tags {error=true, http.status_code=504, otel.status_code=ERROR} and durations of ~14,999,803-15,001,077 us, parented by load-generator GET spans; in trace f2dd787005542001fa63d417d7a7940d the matching frontend server span 'GET' took 15,000,142 us and returned http.status_code=200 while the proxy returned 504.

Compared with a 07:20:00Z baseline (10m p95), frontend's checkout path at 07:44:00Z moved from POST /api/checkout 668.75 ms to 15000 ms, 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' 668.75 ms to 15000 ms and 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' 635.71 ms to 15000 ms, and a 'tcp.connect' span of 15000 ms appears; in the same comparison cart traffic stayed comparable (POST /api/cart 302.84 -> 352.22 ms, grpc CartService/GetCart 175.93 -> 180.74 ms) and GET / stayed fast (156.11 -> 70.00 ms).

For span_name 'oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' the checkout (client) p95 went from 39-88 ms (07:08:54-07:32:54Z) to 15000 ms in 5-minute windows from 07:33:54Z through 07:41:54Z, while the product-catalog (server) p95 for the same span stayed at 1.92-2.00 ms throughout; for the 10-minute window ending 07:44:00Z checkout p95 is 15000 ms versus product-catalog p95 1.995 ms.

frontend's client call rate for 'grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' fell from 5.33-9.42 calls/s (07:10-07:32Z) to 3.99/s at 07:34Z, 0.21/s at 07:36Z and 0 from 07:38Z onward, while product-catalog server spans for oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct continued (88.0 calls in the 10 minutes ending 07:44:00Z, of which checkout contributed 60.76).

chaos-mesh events show Schedule 'otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay' (namespace chaos-mesh) spawning NetworkChaos objects otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay-jj42n, -6rtdg, -bx27q, -x5l64, -b5dxg, -gjgf2, -d9vpw, -26dqc and -hcwrz at 07:30:39Z, 07:31:39Z, 07:32:39Z, 07:33:39Z, 07:34:39Z, 07:35:39Z, 07:36:39Z, 07:37:39Z and 07:38:39Z; each recorded 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9' and 'Time up according to the duration' / 'Successfully recover chaos' about 55 seconds later, and the PodNetworkChaos object 'product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9' in namespace otel-demo was updated on the same cadence.

All 21 otel-demo deployments report READY 1 and AVAILABLE 1 (including frontend-proxy, frontend, checkout and product-catalog), and the pods frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-xh66d, frontend-675fd7b5c5-64blr, checkout-5dccddf8bb-rvrr6 and product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9 are Running/Ready with 0 restarts.

product-catalog's own container log shows normal operation during the window, e.g. 'Product Found' and periodic 'Reloading Product Catalog...' / 'Loaded 10 products' between 07:36:43Z and 07:37:53Z, with no error lines returned.

Service endpoints resolve: product-catalog 100.96.4.247:8080, frontend 100.96.1.181:8080, checkout 100.96.4.114:8080 and frontend-proxy 100.96.4.150:8080, so the timeouts are not an empty-endpoint condition.

The 15 s stalls are caused by a network delay injected on pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9 by the NetworkChaos experiments created by Schedule otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay: caller-side (checkout, frontend) latency for product-catalog calls reached the 15 s ceiling while product-catalog's own server-side spans stayed ~2 ms, i.e. the delay sits on the network path rather than in the application, and the onset (07:32:54Z error-rate rise, 07:33:54Z first 15000 ms p95 window) follows the first injection at 07:30:39Z. The injected delay value, direction and peer/target selector are not readable in this Run, so why checkout's product-catalog calls recovered after ~07:41Z while frontend's product-catalog client spans stayed at zero is unproven; a peer-scoped or connection-state effect is possible.

The proxy error rate remaining above zero at the last data points (1.13/s at 07:43:54Z, 0.63/s at 07:44:54Z, frontend error rate 0.63-0.71/s at 07:43-07:45Z) is a continuation of the same injection, because the Schedule fired on a one-minute cadence and the cluster events available here stop at 07:38:39Z; whether injections continued after 07:38:39Z or the frontend's connections remained stuck afterwards is unverified.

frontend-proxy is not itself broken: its deployment is 1/1 Available, pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-xh66d is Ready with 0 restarts, and it kept serving 200 responses (e.g. 'GET /' 200 via_upstream in 26 ms) while the 504s occurred, so the alert reflects an upstream response timeout rather than a proxy crash or readiness failure.

fraud-detection's restart is not the cause of this alert: its container's last termination was OOMKilled with exitCode 137 finished at 07:26:54Z (restartCount 2) before the error-rate rise at 07:32:54Z, the pod is now Ready, and fraud-detection returned 0 ERROR spans in the 15 minutes ending 07:47:54Z while the failing spans belong to frontend, frontend-proxy and checkout/product-catalog calls.

If this chaos experiment is not intentional, suspend or delete Schedule otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay in namespace chaos-mesh and confirm the frontend-proxy ingress 504 rate returns to its pre-07:32:54Z level; if the 15 s delay is intended as resilience testing, raise the frontend-proxy response timeout or add bounded retries so the proxy does not convert upstream latency into 504 errors.

Preserve and review the NetworkChaos spec for these experiments (latency value, direction, target/peer selector) so the exact scope of the delay on product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9 can be confirmed, since that object's spec was not readable in this Run.

gaps: The chaos-mesh NetworkChaos/Schedule specifications (delay value, direction, target selector, duration) could not be read: those custom resources are not among the kinds this Run may query, so the delay magnitude and whether it is peer-scoped are unverified.

Cluster events returned only timestamps 07:13:32Z-07:38:39Z, so whether Schedule otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay kept injecting NetworkChaos after 07:38:39Z (and whether it is still active) is unknown; this is why the non-zero error rate at 07:43-07:46Z is not fully explained.
frontend container logs returned 0 lines (status no_data) for 07:30:00-07:47:54Z, so frontend-side error text (e.g. gRPC deadline messages) is unavailable.
A networkpolicies query for namespace otel-demo returned no rows with status no_data (not citable), so the absence of a network policy blocking these paths cannot be asserted.

Why frontend's client spans for grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder stay at 15000 ms/error while checkout's own server-side PlaceOrder spans complete in ~390 ms is not explained by the visible spans; the response-path behavior is unknown.
The alerting rule 'RequestErrorRate' was not found in this Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules returned nothing), so the rule expression and threshold behind the alert are unknown.
Jaeger trace data available here ends around 07:40:09Z, so spans after that time (including the tail of the error window) could not be inspected.
The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so deployment/configuration change history for the incident window is unavailable.
next_steps: Have a human review the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay and its NetworkChaos children in namespace chaos-mesh to confirm whether the injected delay is intentional and what delay/peer scope it declares.
If the experiment is not intended, suspend it and re-check service_oteldemo_frontend_proxy error spans and the frontend-proxy ingress 504 rate for recovery.
If the delay is intended, review the frontend-proxy response_timeout (15 s observed) and frontend client deadlines so upstream latency does not surface as 504 errors.
Check the Alertmanager/Prometheus instance that owns the RequestErrorRate rule to record its exact expression and the frontend-proxy series it evaluates.
